one_liner: Hands-on kennel job caring for U.S. Capitol Police working dogs: feeding, medicating, grooming, cleaning kennels, keeping medical records, and driving dogs to vets.
fit_summary: This role requires a year of hands-on canine care (feeding, grooming, health checks, sanitation), and education can't substitute. Daniel's resume has no animal-care work, so it isn't a realistic fit.
eligibility: Open to the public; U.S. citizenship required (no federal status needed).
One year of specialized experience equivalent to CP-03/GS-05 in canine care: sanitation, feeding, grooming, bathing, exercising, health checks, and transporting canines. No education substitution.
Must pass a full field background investigation and serve a one-year probationary period.
Must obtain and maintain a valid REAL ID U.S. driver's license and drive canines to appointments and between facilities.
Must be physically able to lift up to 75 pounds, restrain dogs, and work in adverse weather and kennel conditions.
keywords: liaison between handlers and veterinary personnel
strategy: Skip this one: it requires a year of hands-on canine care, and his resume shows no animal-care work.
A better use of his time: search U.S. Capitol Police, House and Senate postings for legislative affairs or emergency preparedness roles that match his policy interest and IEM background.
resume_bullets: Handled deliveries, conference supplies and office security at IEM (2019–2024).
Helped stand up new COVID-19 mass care sites as on-site assistant to project managers (2021–2022).
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would perform a daily health check on a working canine and what signs would prompt you to call the vet.
Describe a time you handled or restrained a difficult or aggressive dog safely.
How do you keep accurate medical and feeding records when caring for multiple animals?
How would you handle being called in on a weekend or holiday to receive new canines or transport an injured dog?
watch_outs: His resume doesn't meet the mandatory animal-care experience, and education can't substitute.
The job is physically demanding: lifting up to 75 lb, risk of bites and scratches, and exposure to extreme weather and odors.
No telework, plus possible overtime on weekends and holidays, and a commute from Manassas to DC.
Promotion potential tops out at CP-04, so there is no built-in career ladder toward policy work.
